comment: Every web-UI route kind (packages/web-ui/src/lib/routes.ts Route union) with what 'clean' means per role. clean = hard load serves the SPA (200 app, or the row's pinned hardLoad contract), zero console errors, zero failed requests. restricted = the Restricted callout rendered AND no request for the gated resource (the #220 bar). Rows marked pseudo pin contracts outside the Route union (unknown-path fallthrough, reserved API namespaces); scripts/route-walk/contract.mjs validates this file against the router in both directions, including PROFILE_TABS variant parity. {placeholders} are filled from the fixtures file seed.mjs writes. Changing a role expectation is a permissions statement — it gets reviewed like one.

routes.fixture: a channel the member belongs to, plus the built-in general channel
a DM thread with the admin
routes.why: the right-rail activity inspector renders Restricted for a viewer without activity.read on the peer (#214/#220's designed refusal) — the page itself is clean
routes.markerNote: a DM with yourself renders no peer header, and the right-rail peer-activity inspector only renders for a viewer with activity.read — so the two roles genuinely see different views at this URL.

routes.fixture: an objective assigned to the baseline member
the walking member's own profile (every tab incl. manage)
routes.markerNote: tabs are permission-scoped and the router falls back rather than refusing (MemberProfile.tsx effectiveTab): a viewer without members.manage has no activity tab, and nobody has a manage tab on their OWN profile, so those URLs render the overview for that role BY DESIGN. The per-role markers pin that fallback rather than leaving it to be rediscovered.

routes.fixture: a secret bound to the baseline member
a variable bound to the baseline member
the member's own home (root listing + own directory)

routes.pseudo: not a Route union kind — pins the router's unknown-path contract (routes.ts: unknown paths resolve to home)
routes.why: an unknown path falls through to home so stale links don't strand users — in-app via the router, and on hard loads via the Accept-negotiated SPA fallback (run.ts: only an explicit text/html range selects the SPA; API clients get 404). The walker asserts the browser side of that contract

routes.pseudo: not a Route union kind — /enroll is the device-enrolment REST namespace (POST /enroll, GET /enroll/pending), with no GET page of its own
routes.why: in a browser /enroll behaves as an unknown path: home in-app, SPA shell on a hard load via the Accept-negotiated fallback (API clients get 404 — the GET namespace has no route). Adding a real enrolment page later means changing this row under review
